panels.rationale: This is a real patient contrast-enhanced CT (venous phase) image showing active contrast extravasation into the gastric lumen at the gastric cardia, a direct diagnostic finding of active bleeding secondary to Mallory-Weiss syndrome, as explicitly confirmed by the figure caption and article content focused on this target disease. No exclusion criteria apply, the annotation (white arrow) is present, and the finding matches the provided disease-specific vocabulary.

in_text_mentions: Because of hemodynamic instability and a suspicion of internal bleeding, contrast-enhanced CT was performed, which demonstrated active extravasation of contrast into the gastric lumen (Figure 1). An NG tube was subsequently inserted and yielded a bloody aspirate. Because imaging preceded NG tube placement, the mucosal lesion was already present before tube insertion, making iatrogenic injury from the NG tube unlikely.

panels.rationale: Endoscopic image showing a longitudinal mucosal tear at the gastric cardia (arrow), which is the hallmark finding of Mallory-Weiss Syndrome. The caption and article text confirm the diagnosis.
panels.attribution_text: Homma. Mallory-Weiss Syndrome Without Vomiting Following Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation With a Laryngeal Tube.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.110809. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopic image showing MWS Emergent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showing a longitudinal mucosal laceration at the gastric cardia (arrow), consistent with MWS. The laceration is located at the esophagogastric junction. The diagnosis was confirmed after contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated active extravasation into the gastric lumen, followed by nasogastric tube insertion yielding a bloody aspirate. Endoscopic clipping was used to achieve hemostasis MWS: Mallory-Weiss syndrome; CT: computed tomography
in_text_mentions: Emergent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy identified a longitudinal mucosal laceration at the gastric cardia (Figure 2), consistent with MWS and confirming the diagnosis. Endoscopic hemostasis was achieved successfully. Following ICU admission, the hemoglobin level declined to 8.9 g/dL before hemostasis but recovered to 12.8 g/dL after transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells and four units of fresh frozen plasma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Endoscopic view clearly demonstrating a longitudinal mucosal tear at the gastroesophageal junction with adherent clot, consistent with classic Mallory-Weiss syndrome. B: Endoscopic view showing the Mallory-Weiss tear with adherent clot at the esophagogastric junction, consistent with the diagnosed condition. C: Endoscopic view showing the longitudinal mucosal tear and surrounding congested hemorrhagic mucosa as described in the caption. D: Endoscopic view showing fresh blood and possible intervention at the Mallory-Weiss tear site, consistent with active recent bleeding described in the caption.
panels.attribution_text: Gharib et al. Mallory-Weiss tear with intestinal obstruction: case report and literature review.. Journal of surgical case reports 2026. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjag585. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy. A longitudinal mucosal tear is seen at the esophagogastric junction, associated with adherent clot and slight oozing. The surrounding mucosa appears congested and hemorrhagic, with retained altered blood in the stomach. The appearance is consistent with Mallory-Weiss tear with stigmata of active recent bleeding.

in_text_mentions: Endoscopy revealed a longitudinal Mallory-Weiss tear at the gastroesophageal junction measuring 1 × 0.5 mm with active bleeding (Figure 1). Hemostasis was successfully achieved with the application of the first hemoclip (Figure 2) and the second hemoclip (Figure 3). An incidental duodenal polyp was also identified, excised, and biopsied (Figure 4). All images were anonymized to obscure patient-identifying information.
